history.dynasty: Built 1851 (Mathura Seth family; Sri Vaishnava tradition)
history.summary: The Rangaji (Sri Rangji / Ranganath) Temple at Vrindavan, Mathura district — the largest temple devoted to Lord Vishnu in Vrindavan, built in 1851 by the wealthy Seth family of Mathura in a Rajput–South Indian (Dravidian) blend with a six-storey gopuram, 50-ft gold-plated dhwaja stambha, pushkarni tank and gardens; the deity Sri Goda Rangamannar (Vishnu reclining on Sheshanaga) is worshipped in South Indian (Sri Vaishnava) style. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh — no Rangaji temple was found in Lucknow; this record documents the famous Rangaji Temple of Vrindavan, Mathura district. Town corrected; confirm this is the intended row before relying on it.

name: Rangaji Temple
town_description: Vrindavan is the holy temple town in Mathura district on the Yamuna, revered as the childhood playground of Krishna — a dense Vaishnava pilgrimage centre with hundreds of temples including Banke Bihari, the ISKCON Krishna-Balaram Mandir and Prem Mandir, about 150 km from Delhi.

travel.airport: Agra Airport (Kheria), ~60 km; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, ~150 km
travel.railway: Mathura Junction (~12–14 km); Vrindavan has a small station
travel.road: Tatiya Sthan Road, Vrindavan — about 12 km from Mathura; buses and taxis connect Delhi, Agra and Jaipur

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Jal Vihar ceremony and Rath-ka-Mela draw the biggest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer: 8:00 AM–12:45 PM, 4:00–8:00 PM; winter: 5:30–11:00 AM, 4:00–7:30 PM (per UP Tourism — verify locally)
